science.title: New Species of Pygmygoby Discovered at the Edge of the Red Sea’s Unexplored Deep Reefs
science.description: Researchers have described a new species of fish from the northern Red Sea, found at the entrance to a cave on a steep reef slope. Charon’s pygmygoby (Trimma charon) is a small, translucent fish with a broad orange-red stripe, golden spots on its tail, and an unusual four-part eye. The two known specimens measure just 12 and 17 millimetres.

science.title: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
science.description: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish. Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

science.title: Tiny melt traces shed light on the Colorado Plateau's explosive past
science.description: Deep beneath Earth's surface, some minerals hold clues to processes that happened millions of years ago. One such mineral is lawsonite, which forms under high pressure and relatively low temperatures. What makes it significant is its ability to store water within its crystal structure and carry it deep into Earth as tectonic plates move beneath one another.
